transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Anika (Redwood); Diego, Leah, Tom (AuroraCloud)

Summary:
Quick sync on marketplace listing steps, reference architecture for joint solution (Redwood hosted + Aurora managed VPC option), and security/billing handoffs. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: marketplace listing assets; reference architecture and IaC; entitlement and billing; security & compliance; integration test plan; timeline for go-live.

00:00:05 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're going to kick off with quick intros, i'm maya patel, ae on the partnership, jordan and anika from product and se will jump into the tech bits.
00:00:22 Diego: yeah thanks, diego here, partner pm for auroracloud, we handle marketplace ops and want to get the redwood listing live Q4.
00:00:30 Jordan: cool, can i confirm expected deployment models — you want a hosted listing on Aurora's marketplace and also a reference arch for customers to deploy in their VPCs?
00:00:45 Leah: correct, two flavors: 1) marketplace SaaS listing where customers consume redwood-hosted inference via provisioning through aurora billing, and 2) reference architecture for our enterprise customers who want private/dedicated deployments in their Aurora VPCs.
00:01:04 Anika: great, we'll need to outline supported modes, required network flows, and an example terraform/arm template.
00:01:16 Tom: security is critical — we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration points, KMS key handling, and audit logs forwarded to aurora logging. also any encryption at rest details.
00:01:34 Jordan: noted — redwood supports customer-managed KMS, we also have options for dedicated capacity where keys can remain in customer KMS and audit logs. we'll include our standard security checklist but want to confirm aurora's required artifacts.
00:02:02 Diego: i'll summarize aurora asks: listing metadata + copy, logos, pricing tier mapping, billing integration details and if redwood can accept marketplace-driven billing. also a reference arch doc and conformance tests.
00:02:25 Maya: perfect. on billing, we support marketplace billing via marketplace integrations in most cases; we'll need your billing account id and the contract flow.
00:02:36 Leah: ok we'll share that, do you have examples of the listing copy? the marketing team will want the blurb.
00:02:44 Maya: yes i'll send a template with recommended copy and screenshots.
00:02:50 -- 00:03:10 Jordan: Tech deep dive — on the reference arch we propose two topology options: a) Redwood-hosted inference (Redwood API endpoint) with Aurora fronting via marketplace provisioning and optionally VPC egress restricted by customer; b) Dedicated cluster managed by Redwood but sitting in Aurora's customer VPC via a peered or private link for low-latency inference.
00:03:40 Leah: for option b we need details on network requirements, egress ports, and expected latency numbers for 1k qps baseline. can you provide typical throughput/latency with token sizes?
00:03:55 Jordan: rough numbers: for our optimized runtime, 512-token sequences on a dedicated A100-equivalent will typically see p95 latencies around 80-120ms for single-stream loads, throughput scales with batching — we'll include a performance table. note these are approximate and depend on quantization and batch config.
00:04:22 Diego: can you also share the model compatibility list for the listing? customers on aurora will ask which models redwood serves and which are supported in dedicated vs hosted.
00:04:35 Anika: yes we'll attach our curated model catalog and note which ones are compatible with quantized/dedicated runtimes. there may be naming mismatches in the transcript later but we'll provide canonical names.
00:04:50 Tom: about keys and audit logs — we need an architecture for key rotation and how redwood surfaces audit events to aurora. does redwood push logs or do customers pull?
00:05:05 Jordan: we support push to SIEM via secure syslog/HTTP, and customers can pull logs via API. for the marketplace flow, we recommend pushing a subset of audit events to aurora logging for billing reconciliation, while supporting full logs behind customer consent.
00:05:28 Leah: ok. also how do you handle data residency requirements for EU customers? some will require hosting in eu regions only.
00:05:36 Maya: we have regional deployment options and can pin model versions to eu-only clusters; we'll document region availability in the listing.
00:05:48 Diego: great. next item: reference arch doc contents, what do you need?
00:05:55 Jordan: we'll draft a doc that includes: high-level topology diagrams, traffic flows, IAM roles and SAML mappings, network ports, example terraform/helm snippets, performance profile table, security checklist, and a simple conformance test plan (latency/throughput smoke tests).
00:06:20 Leah: that sounds right. can you include an example for KV cache sizing and recommended batching settings? our customers ask about cost tradeoffs.
00:06:31 Anika: yes we'll include guidance — e.g. recommended batch sizes for chat workloads and KV cache policies; quick note — sometimes the transcript engine confuses KV cache for K V cash so we'll make it explicit.
00:06:47 Diego: onboarding + go-to-market — aurora wants joint collateral and a co-branded reference arch. timeline to get listing live by end of october? is that feasible?
00:06:58 Maya: feasible if we get assets this week and review the ref arch early next week; marketplace validation typically takes 2-3 weeks after submission.
00:07:12 Tom: security review timeline — we'll need SOC2 and pen test summaries for marketplace listing. do you have a pre-red-flag list for items that can block listing?
00:07:24 Jordan: common blockers: missing SOC2 link, unclear KMS ownership, no clear audit log export, lack of SSO options. we'll include a checklist to prevent surprises.
00:07:40 Leah: onboarding flow — for SaaS listing, when a customer purchases via aurora marketplace, how is provisioning handled? automatic API key provisioning or manual?
00:07:52 Maya: we can support automatic provisioning via a webhook flow from aurora to create a customer account + API key, or a manual provisioning model for enterprise buyers. we'll need webhook signing keys.
00:08:06 Diego: ok note webhook security requirements.
00:08:12 -- 00:08:40 Jordan: Integration tests — we propose a small conformance suite: auth test, basic infer test, streaming test, billing metering sanity test. we can share a postman/pytest collection.
00:08:55 Leah: yes please, that will help aurora validation team.
00:09:05 Anika: on IaC, we'll provide a terraform module that sets up the minimal networking, IAM roles and a sample deployment for a customer-managed dedicated node. it's mostly param-driven.
00:09:18 Diego: are there any special licensing nuances e.g. if customers bring their own model?
00:09:25 Maya: if customers bring their own model we have a private deployment option and licensing is handled via the dedicated contract; we'll add a note in the ref arch.
00:09:36 Tom: last security quick question — does redwood offer hardware security module (HSM) integrations for key storage?
00:09:44 Jordan: yes, we have KMS/HSM integrations listed, we'll capture supported vendors in the security checklist.
00:09:53 Diego: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
00:09:58 Maya: recap: i'll send listing template + marketing copy; jordan will start reference arch draft; anika will assemble IaC module skeleton; diego/leah to share billing account and logos; tom will provide SOC2 pointer. schedule follow-up week of 9/20.
00:10:18 Leah: sounds good.
00:10:22 -- 00:25:00 free-form discussion / Q&A, small interruptions, clarifications, a few filler words and cross talk. some imperfect transcriptions where product names become 'red wood' or 'aurora cloud' split.
00:25:05 Jordan: one technical note — for low-latency workloads we recommend colocating model weights on the dedicated cluster and enabling continuous batching with a max latency SLO setting. we'll include config examples.
00:25:30 Leah: what's the expected disk requirement for a mid-size model?
00:25:35 Jordan: depends on quantization; e.g. a 13B model quantized to 4-bit may be ~10-12GB, while FP16 could be double; we'll put concrete numbers in the doc.
00:25:50 Diego: ok thanks.
00:26:00 Maya: any blockers from aurora side to start the reference arch draft?
00:26:05 Leah: just permission to use our partner logo and our billing account info, we'll get that over.
00:26:12 Tom: and a pointer to our security contact for detailed questions.
00:26:18 Diego: i'll share that after the call.
00:26:24 -- 00:53:30 wrap up, agree sendables and timeline, casual sign off.
